prompt:
Image 1 is a sprite sheet of one Oakheart warrior, seen from behind, in a 4 by 4 grid on a flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) background. 11 of its figures are finished paintings whose camera, place, size and pose are right; the figures in 5 cells (row 3, column 4; row 3, column 2; row 2, column 3; row 2, column 2; row 2, column 1) are grey clay figures. Repaint every figure of the sheet, the painted ones and the clay ones, as the Oakheart of Image 2 with the changes below, keeping each figure's place in its cell, its pose, its facing, its camera and its size; no clay may remain. The outline changes only where the changes below need it. Keep the 4 by 4 layout, with no grid lines drawn, and the flat pure magenta background.

Image 2 is the approved painted portrait of this Oakheart: use it for its identity, its colours, its materials and its marks, painted in the same hand. Do not copy its head-and-shoulders framing, its dark background, its candlelight or its facing; every figure is the whole Oakheart, small in its cell.

Camera: high above and behind, looking down at about 40 degrees, the way a player looks down at miniatures on a table; orthographic, no perspective. Every figure faces away from us toward the upper right, exactly as in Image 1: we see its back and the top of its head; no face is seen; never at eye level, never seen from the side.

Light: outdoor daylight. A high sun in the upper left of the image lights the top and the upper-left side of the Oakheart with warm highlights; a cool blue-grey sky fill lies in the shadows on the lower-right side. No candlelight, no dramatic dark shadows, nothing glows unless the description says so. No cast shadow on the background.

Painting style: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible directional brushwork, moderate detail, the same hand as the painted portrait reference; a muted earthy palette with the Oakheart's own colours exactly as its portrait shows them; soft painterly edges, small crisp highlights and a thin bright rim of light along the upper-left edges. A strong, simple, readable silhouette that still reads when shrunk to 60 pixels. It is not a cartoon: no cel shading, no thick black outlines, no chibi or big-headed proportions, no glossy 3D render, no pixel art.

The figures: An Oakheart, a walking oak under thornplate, a sacred warrior of the Thornwood: the warrior of Image 2, a broad, heavy, broad-shouldered warrior whose whole body is living grey oak wood, deeply furrowed, with moss in the furrows, armoured in grown thornplate of dark bark plates; not a tree with a face, but a warrior made of oak. Its head is a block of grey furrowed oak with a face only suggested in the grain: two deep dark knotholes for eyes, a long crack running down from the brow across the cheek, a jaw of bark knots. A high helm of dark grown bark plates crowned with a ring of long curved thorns and a fringe of lobed oak leaves around its rim; heavy thornplate pauldrons studded with thorns. It wields an Oak Maul in both hands or one: a long haft of dark oak ending in a huge head of knotted oak root bound with dark iron bands. No shield. Its marks, every one painted clearly: the crown of long curved thorns on the helm; the fringe of lobed oak leaves around the helm's rim; the crack down the face; the moss in the furrows of the grey oak; the bottle-green mantle. Seen from behind and above, the ring of curved thorns on the helm, the leaf fringe, the green mantle down the back and the maul show clearly.

Side colour: a mantle of deep bottle-green cloth (#1F6A50) over both shoulders, under the pauldrons, wrapped across the chest in front and hanging down the back to the backs of the knees: large, clean, unbroken areas that face the sky and the camera, so that a block of Oakhearts reads as that colour from far away; about a third of what the camera sees of each standing figure is this cloth. The green is a deep bottle green, the green of jade in shade, clearly coloured, never grey, slate, olive or yellow-green, never blackish or teal-blue. The rest of the figure stays muted grey oak and dark bark.

The changes, on every figure of the sheet: A tall helm of upright bark planks rising a full head above the brow, ringed by a crown of long curved thorns, with a fringe of oak leaves at its rim, exactly as Image 2. Never a flat cap or a brimmed hat. The face a gaunt skull-like mask of grey oak with a crack across it and moss in the furrows. Tall, realistic proportions: the head with its helm one sixth of the standing height, long arms. The bottle-green mantle large over both shoulders and hanging down the chest, so that from the front it covers a third of the figure.

Scale: An Oakheart is half again as tall as a man and twice as broad; each painted figure covers its clay figure's outline and no more.

The cells, left to right, row by row:
1. (row 1, column 1) standing ready, weight on both feet.
2. (row 1, column 2) standing at ease, weight shifted onto one leg, head turned a little to one side.
3. (row 1, column 3) marching: left foot forward in a long stride, right foot pushing off behind.
4. (row 1, column 4) marching: right foot forward in a long stride, left foot pushing off behind.
5. (row 2, column 1) attack windup: the maul swung far back over the shoulder in both hands, body twisted and coiled (a clay figure in Image 1).
6. (row 2, column 2) the strike: the maul brought down in front in a great blow, lunging forward on the front foot (a clay figure in Image 1).
7. (row 2, column 3) follow-through: the maul swept past and low, body turned with the swing (a clay figure in Image 1).
8. (row 2, column 4) braced: the maul held across the body in both hands, knees bent.
9. (row 3, column 1) recoiling from a hit: knocked back, head snapped back, arms thrown out, one foot stepping back.
10. (row 3, column 2) falling backward, knees buckling, about halfway to the ground (a clay figure in Image 1).
11. (row 3, column 3) lying dead on the ground on its back, limbs loose.
12. (row 3, column 4) lying dead on the ground face down, a different sprawl (a clay figure in Image 1).
13. (row 4, column 1) fleeing away from the enemy: lumbering hard, the maul dropped, looking back over the shoulder.
14. (row 4, column 2) fleeing: the other foot forward, arms swinging, looking back.
15. (row 4, column 3) victory: the maul raised high overhead in one hand, the other fist raised.
16. (row 4, column 4) no figure: only the oak maul lying flat on the ground, as dropped.

Background: one flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) colour fills the whole image with no gradient, texture, floor, vignette or shadow; at least 24 pixels of clean background between any two figures and around the edges. No pink, magenta, violet or purple anywhere on the creature.

Never: text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, borders, frames, signatures, logos; a floor, ground, scenery or cast shadows; blood; extra figures; cropped or overlapping figures.
